newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia govt will not lift borrowing to pay wages. [CORRECTED 12:45 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Russia govt will not lift borrowing to pay wages. [CORRECTED 12:45 gmt]

text.p: Russia's federal government will not increase borrowing to finance its promised payment of public-sector wage arrears, and wants Treasury bill yields to fall further, First Deputy Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin said on Friday.
"Borrowing will be within the framework set in the 1997 budget limits, and will not exceed them," he told a news conference.

The federal government owes 7.7 trillion roubles in unpaid public-sector wages and has promised to pay 50 percent of wage arrears of those regional governments which cannot cope on their own, he said. Regional governments owe a total of 25.6 trillion roubles in unpaid wages, the finance ministry said in a statement.
President Boris Yeltsin this month ordered the government to pay all wage arrears by January 1 next year, including about five trillion roubles to the military by September 1.
The payments will be funded by privatisation revenues, cuts in the number of government employees and improved tax collection, Kudrin said.

Yeltsin has authorised the government to decide which companies should be privatised and when, and the finance ministry is now working on a list of companies in which the government will sell controlling stakes, he said.
(Corrects to make clear the government as a whole and not the finance ministry is handling the privatisation).
